mainTopic: Who brings פסח שני and what it is: הורצה for the traveler on a דרך רחוקה, whether women bring it, and the three-way dispute over כרת for skipping the first or second פסח.
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבי עקיבא's comparison: a person on a דרך רחוקה is like a טמא. This was a challenge to רב נחמן, who holds that a פסח offered for the traveler counts (הורצה). רב נחמן answers that רבי עקיבא follows his own view that we do not slaughter for a טמא שרץ, a view רב נחמן rejects. A ברייתא then lists who brings פסח שני. After correcting its question, the ברייתא says the תורה names the traveler to exempt him from כרת, and this fits רב נחמן's view of הורצה. The גמרא resolves a contradiction about whether women bring פסח שני by assigning the two ברייתות to different תנאים. Next comes a three-way dispute about כרת. רבי holds that פסח שני is its own holiday. רבי נתן holds that it is only a make-up. רבי חנניא בן עקביא holds that it repairs the first. All three learn their view from one פסוק. The amud ends by asking how we know that חטאו ישא means כרת, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא compares a distant traveler to an impure person
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי עקיבא's ברייתא: a person on a דרך רחוקה is like a טמא. Both are able in principle to bring the פסח, but the תורה holds them back. This challenges רב נחמן's ruling of הורצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as a טמא is someone who could bring the offering but does not, because the תורה stops him, so too a person on a דרך רחוקה could bring it but does not, because the תורה stops him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי עקיבא's comparison. It was brought to challenge רב נחמן, who said that a פסח offered for a person on a דרך רחוקה is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a traveler is treated exactly like a טמא, then the תורה has disqualified him from the first פסח. That suggests that slaughtering for him would not work, which contradicts רב נחמן's view of הורצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure person
He has the ability / means in his hand
A distant journey (one of the תורה's cases for פסח שני)
Also

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the tail end of a ברייתא that began on the previous amud. It is not a new statement. It is the challenge that רב נחמן must answer in the next step.

phrases.english: Just as an impure person,
has the ability to do it, yet does not do it,
phrases.notes: The תורה stops him from bringing it.

phrases.english: so too a distant journey,
is one who has the ability to do it, yet does not do it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה טָמֵא, שֶׁסִּפֵּק בְּיָדוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת וְאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge against רב נחמן that began on the previous amud.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that a פסח offered for one on a דרך רחוקה is accepted (הורצה).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Equating the traveler with a טמא implies that he is disqualified from the first פסח, so an offering made for him should not count.

steps.title: רב נחמן: רבי עקיבא follows his own view on a טמא שרץ
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that רבי עקיבא holds we do not slaughter for a טמא שרץ. רב נחמן holds like the opinion that we do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן would say to you: רבי עקיבא is following his own reasoning. He holds that we do not slaughter and sprinkle for someone impure from a שרץ. But I hold like the opinion that we do slaughter and sprinkle for someone impure from a שרץ.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן deflects the challenge. He shows that רבי עקיבא's comparison depends on a view that רב נחמן himself does not accept.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טמא שרץ can immerse and be pure by nighttime when the פסח is eaten. Even so, רבי עקיבא says we cannot offer for him, because he is unfit at the time of the זריקה. Once רב נחמן holds that we may offer for a טמא שרץ, the comparison works the other way: the traveler, who can arrive by night, is also acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own (consistent) reasoning
We slaughter and sprinkle the blood
A person impure from touching a dead creeping animal (purifiable by evening)
I hold / it is my view

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the הורצה debate about the traveler depends on a broader question: does being unfit at the time of the זריקה (but fit by nightfall) disqualify someone?

phrases.english: And Rav Nachman would say to you:
Rabbi Akiva follows his own reasoning,
for he holds: we do not slaughter and sprinkle
on behalf of one impure from a sheretz.
But I hold like the one who said:
we slaughter and sprinkle on behalf of one impure from a sheretz.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי עקיבא's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The challenge depends on a disputed opinion (רבי עקיבא לטעמיה).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא's comparison binds everyone, so the traveler is disqualified.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison works only for someone who holds אין שוחטין על טמא שרץ. רב נחמן holds the opposite, so his view of הורצה stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists everyone who brings פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists the people who bring פסח שני. The list includes people who are impure, people who missed it by accident, people who were forced, people who skipped it on purpose, and the טמא and the person on a דרך רחוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: These are the ones who bring the second פסח: male and female זבים, male and female מצורעים, נדות and men who had relations with נדות, women after childbirth, those who missed it by mistake, those who were forced, those who skipped it on purpose, and the טמא and one who was on a distant journey.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support רב נחמן. This step sets up the list, and the next steps draw the proof from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list shows that anyone who missed the first פסח, for any reason, brings פסח שני. That raises an obvious question: why does the תורה single out specific cases at all?

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages taught (introduces a ברייתא)
The second (פסח שני, on 14 Iyar)
Men and women with a זיבה discharge
People afflicted with צרעת
Unintentional, forced, and intentional

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be surprised that even מזידין (people who skipped on purpose) bring פסח שני. This ברייתא holds that פסח שני is a make-up for everyone, not only for the cases the תורה names.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
These are the ones who observe the second [Pesach]:
zavim and zavot,
male lepers and female lepers,
menstruating women, men who had relations with them, and women after childbirth,
those who missed it unwittingly, those forced, and those who did so intentionally,
and one impure, and one who was on a distant journey.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, אֵלּוּ שֶׁעוֹשִׂין אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב נחמן's position.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן's view that a פסח offered for one on a דרך רחוקה is accepted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about who brings פסח שני.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks why impurity is mentioned
steps.stepSummary: Since everyone who misses the first פסח brings the second, the ברייתא asks why the תורה specifically mentions a טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the תורה say "טמא"?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a question. If everyone brings פסח שני, what does the תורה gain by naming specific cases?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes that a case named in the תורה must teach something special. Since the general rule already covers everyone, the specific mention seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why was it stated (in the פסוק)?

phrases.english: If so, why is "impure" stated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a question based on its list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תורה's explicit mention of a טמא comes to teach.

steps.title: The גמרא objects: the impurity case is obviously needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised by the question. Mentioning טמא is clearly needed: it teaches that a טמא may not bring the first פסח even if he wants to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is it stated?! Because if he wants to bring it on the first פסח, we do not let him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא's question. The case of טמא has an obvious purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טמא case is not mentioned only to send him to פסח שני. It teaches that he is actively barred from the first פסח. So the question "why is טמא stated" cannot be right as written.

keyTerms.meaning: He wants to do (it)
On the first (פסח)
We do not let him

phrases.english: Why is it stated?!
For if he wants to perform it on the first,
we do not let him!

steps.triggerLanguage: לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר?! דְּאִי בָּעֵי לְמִיעְבַּד בָּרִאשׁוֹן לָא שָׁבְקִינַן לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא's question in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's question "why is טמא stated?"
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The טמא case clearly teaches something: he is barred from the first פסח. So the question is baseless as written.

steps.title: Corrected reading: the דרך רחוקה is mentioned to exempt from כרת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the question so that it asks about דרך רחוקה. The answer is that the תורה mentions it to exempt the traveler from כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: If so, why is "a distant journey" stated? To exempt him from כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the ברייתא's wording. Now the question is about the traveler, and the ברייתא answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The traveler is not actively barred from the first פסח the way a טמא is; a פסח could have been offered for him. So naming him in the תורה must teach something else: even though he missed the first פסח, he is exempt from the כרת that normally comes for skipping it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a correction)
To exempt him
Spiritual excision, the punishment for not bringing the פסח

phrases.english: Rather: if so,
why is "on a distant journey" stated?
To exempt him from karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: אִם כֵּן, לָמָּה נֶאֱמַר ״בְּדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection in step 5 by rereading the ברייתא's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual correction of the ברייתא's question.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא asked about דרך רחוקה. Its purpose is to exempt the traveler from כרת, not to bar him from the first פסח.

steps.title: This fits the view that the offering is accepted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that this ברייתא follows the opinion that a פסח offered for the traveler is accepted (הורצה), which is רב נחמן's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows the one who said: it was accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the conclusion of the proof. The ברייתא matches רב נחמן's view of הורצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה's only purpose in naming the traveler is to exempt him from כרת. So he is not disqualified from the first פסח the way a טמא is. It follows that if they offered for him, it counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It was accepted / he achieved atonement through it
In accordance with the one who said

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן holds that a פסח slaughtered for someone on a דרך רחוקה counts (הורצה). He deflects רבי עקיבא's comparison as following רבי עקיבא's own view on טמא שרץ. A ברייתא supports him: the תורה mentions the traveler only to exempt him from כרת, not to disqualify him.

phrases.english: And this is in accordance with the one who said: it was accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final inference from the corrected ברייתא in support of רב נחמן.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא supports רב נחמן: a פסח offered for one on a דרך רחוקה is accepted.

steps.title: Are women really obligated in פסח שני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier ברייתא, which listed women among those who bring פסח שני. Another ברייתא learns from "איש איש" that the extra cases covered by פסח שני are men.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is a woman obligated in the second פסח? But a ברייתא taught: I might think only a טמא מת or someone far away does the second פסח. Where do we learn זבים, מצורעים, and men who had relations with a נדה? The verse says "איש איש" ("any man").
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the list from the earlier ברייתא, which included women. A different ברייתא seems to say that פסח שני is only for men.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second ברייתא uses the doubled word "איש איש" to add more people to פסח שני beyond the טמא מת and the traveler. Every case it adds is a man: זבים, מצורעים, and men who were with a נדה. Since the word means "man," women seem left out, which contradicts the first ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
Is she really obligated? (a challenging question)
Men with a זיבה discharge, which makes them טמא
People with צרעת (a skin affliction that makes them טמא)
Men who had relations with a נדה and became טמא
"Any man": a doubled word used to include more cases

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether women bring the first פסח. It is only about whether they are obligated in the second one.

phrases.english: Is a woman obligated in the second [Pesach]?
But wasn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל לֹא יְהוּ עוֹשִׂין אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי
phrases.english: I might think that none perform the second

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא טְמֵא נֶפֶשׁ וְשֶׁהָיָה בְּדֶרֶךְ רְחוֹקָה.
phrases.english: except one impure from a corpse and one who was on a distant journey.
Zavim, lepers, and men who had relations with menstruating women: from where [do we know they bring it]?
The verse says: "any man (ish ish)."
phrases.notes: The doubled word includes more cases, but only men.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשָּׁה בַּשֵּׁנִי מִי מִיחַיְּיבָא? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא from step 3 and challenges its inclusion of women.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier ברייתא's inclusion of women among those who bring פסח שני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא extends פסח שני only through "איש," which means "man," so women seem excluded.

steps.title: The two ברייתות follow different תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The first ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, who holds women are obligated in פסח שני. The second follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון, who hold they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי יוסי; that one follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה earlier in the פרק, רבי יוסי says we slaughter a פסח שני for a woman. רבי יהודה says she is only included along with others, and רבי שמעון says we do not slaughter for her at all. So the list with women follows רבי יוסי, and the "איש"-only ברייתא follows the other two.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (a standard answer formula)
This one ... that one: splitting two sources between two opinions
The תנא who holds women are obligated in פסח שני

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
This [baraita] follows Rabbi Yosei,
that one follows Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the two sources to different תנאים (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות seemed to agree, so they appeared to contradict each other about women.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא that includes women follows רבי יוסי. The "איש איש" ברייתא follows רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether a woman is obligated in פסח שני is a dispute: רבי יוסי says yes, while רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say no.

steps.title: Three opinions on כרת for skipping פסח ראשון or פסח שני
steps.stepSummary: רבי says there is כרת for skipping either פסח. רבי נתן says there is כרת only for the first. רבי חנניא בן עקביא says there is כרת for skipping the first only if the person also does not bring the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: one is liable to כרת for the first and liable to כרת for the second, says רבי. רבי נתן says: liable to כרת for the first and exempt for the second. רבי חנניא בן עקביא says: even for the first he is liable to כרת only if he did not do the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with a three-way argument about when someone who skips פסח gets כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי treats each פסח as carrying its own כרת. רבי נתן says the תורה gives כרת only for the first, so skipping the second brings no כרת. רבי חנניא בן עקביא goes further: even after skipping the first, the person can still avoid כרת by bringing the second, so כרת applies only if he skips both.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off: the punishment for deliberately skipping the קרבן פסח
The first פסח, on the 14th of ניסן
The second פסח, on the 14th of אייר
Exempt (here, from כרת)
The תנא who holds the second פסח can save a person from כרת for the first

steps.confusionAlert: "Liable for the second" in רבי's view means someone who had to bring פסח שני (for example, because he was טמא at the first) and deliberately skipped it.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One is liable to karet for [skipping] the first,

phrases.aramaic: וְחַיָּיב כָּרֵת עַל הַשֵּׁנִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.
phrases.english: and liable to karet for [skipping] the second; these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Natan says:

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב כָּרֵת עַל הָרִאשׁוֹן, וּפָטוּר עַל הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: One is liable to karet for the first, and exempt for the second.
Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya says:
Even for the first, one is not liable to karet

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן לֹא עָשָׂה אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: unless he did not perform the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חַיָּיב כָּרֵת עַל הָרִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the כרת rules for פסח ראשון and פסח שני.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי: כרת for each פסח. רבי נתן: כרת only for the first. רבי חנניא בן עקביא: כרת for the first only if he also skips the second.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute shapes the rest of the sugya, which will explain how each תנא understands the relationship between the two פסחים.

steps.title: רבי and רבי נתן stay consistent: the גר and the קטן
steps.stepSummary: רבי and רבי נתן argue the same way about a גר or קטן who became obligated between the two פסחים. רבי obligates them in פסח שני. רבי נתן says that whoever was not obligated in the first is not obligated in the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: They follow their own reasoning, as a ברייתא taught: a גר who converted between the two פסחים, and a קטן who came of age between the two פסחים, must bring פסח שני, says רבי. רבי נתן says: whoever is obligated in the first is obligated in the second; whoever is not obligated in the first is not obligated in the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רבי and רבי נתן each hold one consistent view, using a second argument between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי, פסח שני stands on its own: it has its own כרת and its own obligation, so even someone who first became obligated after פסח ראשון must bring it. For רבי נתן, פסח שני only exists for someone who already owed the first one. That is why it has no separate כרת, and why a new גר or a newly adult קטן does not bring it.

keyTerms.meaning: And they follow their own reasoning (each is consistent with his other rulings)
A convert who converted
A minor who became an adult (בר מצוה)
Obligated, required

steps.whatToRemember: רבי treats פסח שני as an independent obligation, with its own כרת and including newcomers. רבי נתן treats it as tied to the first: no separate כרת, and only for those who already owed the first פסח.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the sugya builds on this, explaining each opinion as a different view of what פסח שני is.

phrases.english: And they follow their own reasoning.
As it was taught in a baraita:
A convert who converted between the two Pesachs,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן קָטָן שֶׁהִגְדִּיל בֵּין שְׁנֵי פְסָחִים —
phrases.english: and similarly a minor who came of age between the two Pesachs,

phrases.aramaic: חַיָּיב לַעֲשׂוֹת פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.
phrases.english: is obligated to perform the second Pesach; these are the words of Rabbi.
Rabbi Natan says:
Whoever is obligated in the first is obligated in the second;

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין זָקוּק לָרִאשׁוֹן — אֵין זָקוּק לַשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: whoever is not obligated in the first is not obligated in the second.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the dispute in step 10 by showing the same two תנאים argue the same way in a related case.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי's and רבי נתן's views on כרת for פסח שני come from a consistent understanding of what פסח שני is.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a גר or קטן who became obligated between the two פסחים.

steps.title: What is the root of their argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what underlying idea causes רבי, רבי נתן, and רבי חנניא בן עקביא to disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what basic idea is behind the three opinions about כרת. This question sets up the next steps, where each opinion's reasoning is explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 gave us three different rulings about כרת. Now the גמרא wants the principle behind each ruling. The answer will be each תנא's view of what פסח שני actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: On what do they disagree? (asks for the root of an argument)

phrases.english: On what do they disagree?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking what deeper idea their argument really comes down to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle behind the dispute stated in Step 10 and paralleled in Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The conceptual basis that produces each of the three rulings about כרת.

steps.title: רבי: the second פסח is its own holiday
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that פסח שני is an independent holiday, not just a make-up for the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds: the second פסח is a holiday on its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי's reasoning: פסח שני is a separate holiday with its own obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פסח שני is its own holiday, then skipping it is its own sin, so it carries its own כרת, just like the first. This also explains Step 11: a גר or קטן who became obligated between the two must bring פסח שני, since it is a new obligation of its own.

keyTerms.meaning: A holiday on its own, an independent festival
Holds, is of the opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi holds:
the second [פסח] is a festival in its own right.
phrases.notes: So skipping either one is a separate sin with כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סָבַר: שֵׁנִי רֶגֶל בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: First part of the answer to the question in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי, פסח שני is an independent festival, so it has its own obligation and its own כרת.

steps.title: רבי נתן: the second פסח is only a make-up
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן holds that פסח שני is only a make-up for the first, and it cannot undo a deliberate failure to bring the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן holds: the second פסח is a make-up for the first. But it does not fix the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי נתן's reasoning: פסח שני is only a second chance to bring what was owed on the first, not its own holiday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since פסח שני is not its own obligation, skipping it brings no כרת of its own. And since it does not 'fix' the first, a person who deliberately skipped the first still gets כרת even if he brings the second. This also explains Step 11: someone who was not obligated in the first has nothing to make up.

keyTerms.meaning: Make-up, a compensation for something missed
To repair or fix
It does not repair it

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי נתן with רבי חנניא בן עקביא. Both see פסח שני as linked to the first. But for רבי נתן it does NOT remove the כרת of a deliberate skip, while for רבי חנניא בן עקביא it DOES.

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan holds:
the second is a make-up for the first.
phrases.notes: It is not an independent obligation.

phrases.english: But as for repairing the first, it does not repair it.
phrases.notes: A deliberate skip of the first still carries כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נָתָן סָבַר: שֵׁנִי תַּשְׁלוּמִין דְּרִאשׁוֹן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second part of the answer to Step 12, contrasting with רבי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי נתן, פסח שני is only a make-up. It has no כרת of its own and does not cancel the כרת for a deliberate skip of the first.

steps.title: רבי חנניא בן עקביא: the second פסח repairs the first
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן עקביא holds that פסח שני is a repair for the first. Bringing it removes the כרת for missing the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא בן עקביא holds: the second פסח is a repair for the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי חנניא בן עקביא's reasoning: פסח שני fixes the failure to bring the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the second can fix the first, the כרת for skipping the first only takes effect if the person also misses the second. This matches his ruling in Step 10: כרת applies only if he skipped both.

keyTerms.meaning: A repair, a fix

steps.whatToRemember: Three views of פסח שני: רבי says it is its own holiday, so each one carries its own כרת. רבי נתן says it is a make-up that cannot erase the first's כרת. רבי חנניא בן עקביא says it is a repair that can erase the first's כרת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Chananya ben Akavya holds:
the second is a repair for the first.
phrases.notes: Bringing the second removes the כרת of the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי חֲנַנְיָא בֶּן עֲקַבְיָא סָבַר: שֵׁנִי תַּקַּנְתָּא דְרִאשׁוֹן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third and final part of the answer to Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רבי חנניא בן עקביא, פסח שני repairs the first, so כרת applies only if both are missed.

steps.title: All three learn from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that all three תנאים derive their views from one פסוק about the man who is טהור and not on a journey.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all three of them learned from one verse: 'But the man who is pure and was not on a journey.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces the one פסוק that all three opinions are built on. This sets up the next step, where each תנא's reading is explained, starting with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we had the logic of each view. Now the גמרא shows that each view also comes from the text of the תורה. The argument will turn on how to read the words of this פסוק (במדבר ט:יג).

keyTerms.meaning: All three of them
They expounded one verse
Ritually pure

phrases.english: And all three of them expounded one verse:
'But the man who is pure,'
'and was not on a journey.'
phrases.notes: The verse goes on to discuss refraining from the פסח and כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the logic of the three views to their source in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All three opinions are derived from במדבר ט:יג.

steps.title: רבי's reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads the first half of the verse as כרת for missing the first פסח, and the second half as כרת for missing the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds: 'and refrains from doing the פסח, and will be cut off' refers to one who did not bring it on the first. Or also: 'he did not bring the offering of ה׳ in its time' refers to the second.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how רבי reads the פסוק: one phrase gives כרת for the first פסח, and another phrase gives כרת for the second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי splits the verse into two separate cases joined by 'or also'. Missing the first is כרת, and missing the second is also כרת. This fits his view that פסח שני is its own holiday with its own penalty.

keyTerms.meaning: And refrains, holds back from
And will be cut off (כרת)
Or also, alternatively
In its appointed time

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows רבי's view of כרת for either פסח comes straight from the wording of the פסוק. The readings of רבי נתן and רבי חנניא בן עקביא come next in the sugya.

phrases.english: Rabbi holds:
'and refrains from doing the פסח, that soul will be cut off'
means that he did not do it on the first.
phrases.notes: This is the first case that gets כרת.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי: ״קׇרְבַּן ה׳ לֹא הִקְרִיב בְּמוֹעֲדוֹ״, בַּשֵּׁנִי.
phrases.english: Or also: 'he did not bring the offering of ה׳ in its appointed time' means on the second.
phrases.notes: Second, separate case of כרת. Either one alone brings כרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי סָבַר: וְחָדַל לַעֲשׂוֹת הַפֶּסַח וְנִכְרְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining each תנא's reading of the verse introduced in Step 16, starting with רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי reads the verse as two separate sources of כרת: one for the first פסח and one for the second.

steps.title: How do we know 'bear his sin' means כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source showing that the phrase חטאו ישא refers to the punishment of כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that this phrase, 'he shall bear his sin,' means כרת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to question one link in רבי's reading. It wants proof that the words חטאו ישא mean כרת. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי's whole reading depends on חטאו ישא meaning כרת, because that is how he gets כרת for missing the second פסח. The פסוק itself does not say the word כרת in that half. It only says 'he shall bear his sin,' which could mean some other punishment. So the גמרא asks for a source before it accepts רבי's reading.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? (Asks for the source of an idea.)
That this (points to the phrase being discussed)
He shall bear his sin (a phrase in the פסוק about the person who skips the פסח)
Spiritual 'cutting off,' a very severe heavenly punishment

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether רבי is right about פסח שני. The גמרא is only asking about the meaning of the words חטאו ישא. Those same words could, in principle, mean a lighter punishment, such as death by heaven (מיתה בידי שמים).
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי's view that you get כרת for missing the second פסח stands or falls on this point. If חטאו ישא does not mean כרת, his reading of the second half of the פסוק falls apart.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that this
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: phrase 'he shall bear his sin' means כרת?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the assumption behind רבי's reading in step 17, that חטאו ישא means כרת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source proving that the phrase חטאו ישא means the punishment of כרת.
